- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% relative to sentiment-driven highs.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is bearish (low sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price drops — model tends to overreact; cap upward momentum at 10–15% above recent 7-day average.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates >15% from 30-day moving average, adjust toward historical mean (last 30 days) with decay factor of 0.8 per day.
- Lag correction: if sentiment is strong but price hasn’t moved yet, delay forecast peak by 1–2 days; if sentiment weakens, accelerate downward correction.
- Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is flat (0.3–0.7) — model overfits noise; use 30-day smoothing filter for price projections.
